cross_references.title: Inalienable Rights (including privacy)
cross_references.note: Section 1 includes an explicit right to privacy. Section 13 protects against unreasonable searches and seizures. Together they form California's privacy-and-security framework, which is broader than federal protections.

cross_references.title: Truth in Evidence (Proposition 8, 1982)
cross_references.note: Section 28(f)(2) requires California courts to follow federal exclusionary rule standards in criminal cases. This limits the practical effect of § 13's broader protections for purposes of suppressing evidence, while leaving the underlying right intact.

cross_references.title: Fourth Amendment — Search and Seizure
cross_references.note: Section 13 tracks the Fourth Amendment's language closely but is independently enforceable and can be interpreted more broadly by California courts.

cross_references.title: Civil Action for Deprivation of Rights
cross_references.note: Section 1983 provides a federal cause of action for violations of constitutional rights by state actors. Fourth Amendment violations are actionable under § 1983. State § 13 violations may support parallel state claims.
